highlights.title: Agent-Editing World Model: Rethinking World Modeling for LLM Agents
highlights.summary: The Agent-Editing World Model (AEWM) treats reasoning and actions as the drivers of future task progress, adding an Action Judge to classify decisions and a State Revision module to edit noisy continuations.
highlights.detail: AEWM addresses task‑state contamination, where outdated plans linger in an agent's history and skew later choices. Unlike prior world models that predict tool outputs, AEWM focuses on how actions reshape the task state, improving decision quality in long‑horizon tasks.

highlights.title: Mizar: A 159M-Parameter Audio-Language Model for Audio Understanding
highlights.summary: Mizar is a 159.3 M‑parameter audio‑language model that attains a 52.92 % mean accuracy on the MM benchmark across five random seeds.
highlights.detail: The model couples a compact CED‑Small audio encoder with SmolLM2‑135M via a frequency‑merging mapper and follows a three‑stage training pipeline: alignment, audio‑dependent fine‑tuning, and post‑training to reinforce weak skills while preserving learned capabilities.

highlights.title: Controlling Collectives of AI Agents in Reasoning Space with Spatial Transformers
highlights.summary: COMPASS is a decentralized multi‑robot architecture that uses a spatial‑transformer feedback token to coordinate large fleets of LLM‑controlled robots, achieving cohesive flocking formations.
highlights.detail: Each robot locally generates feedback by aggregating multi‑hop messages across the fleet, allowing structured diversity in commands to cancel biases. Experiments show performance gains over centralized frontier policies and language‑only communication baselines.

highlights.title: Flamingo: On Load Balancing in DAG-based Consensus Protocols
highlights.summary: Flamingo introduces a load‑balancing layer for certified DAG‑based BFT consensus that periodically migrates client accounts away from overloaded validators while preserving Byzantine safety.
highlights.detail: Flamingo operates on both the ordering and execution layers of DAG‑based BFT protocols. Account migrations are recorded only in the committed log, preserving safety despite Byzantine actors. The approach adapts to skewed client submission patterns and heterogeneous validator capacities.

highlights.title: Audio Spectrum Analyzer on an ESP32 Display Board
highlights.summary: Hackaday features a DIY audio spectrum analyzer built on an ESP32 display board, demonstrating compact real‑time spectrum analysis.
highlights.detail: The project combines the ESP32's processing power with a small LCD to visualize frequency content, offering an accessible platform for hobbyists interested in signal‑processing applications.

items.title: Introducing MentalHealthBench
items.summary: MentalHealthBench is an expert‑informed benchmark for measuring helpful and safe AI responses in realistic mental‑health conversations.
items.detail: The benchmark provides a standardized evaluation suite that captures nuanced conversational dynamics, enabling developers to assess both the utility and safety of AI assistants in sensitive mental‑health contexts.

items.title: Mercury 2.5 LLM hits 770 tokens per second
items.summary: Mercury 2.5 LLM processes 770 tokens per second, a notable speed improvement for the model family.
items.detail: The throughput measurement reflects optimized inference pipelines, making Mercury 2.5 suitable for latency‑sensitive applications while maintaining the model's existing capability profile.

items.title: Advancing Private AI Compute with secure, server-side memory
items.summary: DeepMind added private, server‑side memory to its Private AI Compute platform, enabling secure personal AI workloads on the server.
items.detail: The new memory architecture keeps user data encrypted and isolated on the server, reducing the need for client‑side storage while preserving privacy guarantees for personal AI services.

items.title: Bringing Private Processing to Meta AI Glasses
items.summary: Meta announced private processing on AI glasses, keeping personal context on‑device while delivering continuous AI assistance throughout the day.
items.detail: By handling sensitive data locally, the glasses aim to reduce reliance on phones and improve user presence, while still leveraging cloud‑based models for advanced perception tasks.

items.title: ChatGPT Ads expands to Southeast Asia and Taiwan
items.summary: ChatGPT Ads is expanding to Southeast Asia and Taiwan, now covering businesses in over 60 countries.
items.detail: The rollout gives eligible advertisers new channels to reach audiences across the region, extending the platform's ad‑targeting capabilities beyond its initial markets.

items.title: Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech says hello
items.summary: DeepMind released Gemini 3.8 with an added text‑to‑speech feature that can vocalize generated content.
items.detail: The new speech capability complements Gemini's existing multimodal abilities, allowing developers to integrate spoken output into applications without requiring separate TTS services.

items.title: Harvey turns legal context into stronger drafts with GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: OpenAI's GPT‑6 Astra produces more structured, context‑aware legal drafts, letting lawyers focus on strategy rather than document formatting.
items.detail: The model leverages legal domain data to improve clause organization and relevance, reducing manual editing time while maintaining compliance with jurisdiction‑specific requirements.

items.title: Audio Spectrum Analyzer on an ESP32 Display Board
items.summary: Hackaday features a DIY audio spectrum analyzer built on an ESP32 display board, demonstrating compact real‑time spectrum analysis.
items.detail: The project combines the ESP32's processing power with a small LCD to visualize frequency content, offering an accessible platform for hobbyists interested in signal‑processing applications.

items.title: Security updates for Wednesday
items.summary: LWN reports security updates for numerous Linux distributions, including patches for coreutils, PostgreSQL, Chromium, and kernel packages across AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Red Hat, SUSE, and Ubuntu.
items.detail: The updates address a range of vulnerabilities, from privilege escalation to remote code execution, and are recommended for immediate deployment to maintain system integrity.

items.title: Systemd v262 released
items.summary: Systemd v262 adds static binary builds for containers, kernel coredump socket support from Linux 6.17, and OpenSSL 4 compatibility.
items.detail: Static linking reduces the footprint for containerized environments. The new coredump socket protocol integrates kernel‑level core dump handling introduced in Linux 6.17. OpenSSL 4 updates cryptographic support. Numerous other minor improvements are listed in the release notes.

items.title: Critical WordPress RCE vulnerability announced
items.summary: A critical unauthenticated RCE bug in WordPress get_page_template() was disclosed, with patches back‑ported to branches as old as 4.7; ClassicPress is also vulnerable and lacks a fix.
items.detail: The flaw resides in the template resolution logic and can be triggered without authentication under specific conditions. Patches are available for the current WordPress branch and back‑ported to versions as old as 4.7. ClassicPress inherits the same code path but has not released a fix yet, so users should apply the WordPress update promptly.

items.title: Critical security vulnerabilities in the Radicle network protocol
items.summary: Radicle disclosed two critical protocol flaws that break confidentiality and peer authentication, enabling network eavesdropping and node‑ID spoofing to read private repositories.
items.detail: The confidentiality issue allows any observer on the network path to read exchanged data, while the broken authentication lets an attacker spoof node IDs and access private repositories. Exploiting both flaws together enables full repository theft after a single observation. Radicle recommends immediate patching once available.

items.title: [$] Ideas on modernizing the open-source desktop
items.summary: Scott Jenson urged open‑source projects at Akademy 2026 to move beyond the traditional WIMP desktop model and experiment with new UI/UX approaches.
items.detail: Jenson, with experience at Apple and Google, argued that the desktop UI paradigm has stagnated. He suggested exploring alternative interaction models beyond windows, icons, menus, and pointers. The talk aimed to inspire KDE and other open‑source communities to lead redesign efforts.

items.title: Flamingo: On Load Balancing in DAG-based Consensus Protocols
items.summary: Flamingo introduces a load‑balancing layer for certified DAG‑based BFT consensus that periodically migrates client accounts away from overloaded validators while preserving Byzantine safety.
items.detail: Flamingo operates on both the ordering and execution layers of DAG‑based BFT protocols. Account migrations are recorded only in the committed log, preserving safety despite Byzantine actors. The approach adapts to skewed client submission patterns and heterogeneous validator capacities.

items.title: xTier: Intelligent Tiering for CXL-Enabled Memory
items.summary: xTier implements a kernel‑resident learned memory‑tiering system for CXL‑enabled servers, using eBPF‑hooked PEBS events and a compact quantized MLP to score pages with microsecond latency.
items.detail: xTier runs entirely in kernel space, avoiding userspace‑kernel crossing overhead. eBPF programs attached to PEBS events collect page‑access samples, which a quantized multi‑layer perceptron scores in microseconds. After convergence, the system stabilizes placement for the current workload phase, reducing sampling overhead.

items.title: EBRL: Asynchronous Embodied RL by Multi-Grained Resource Management
items.summary: EBRL presents an asynchronous embodied‑RL system that pipelines rollout and training while a fine‑grained manager dynamically allocates CPU cores and GPU streaming multiprocessors based on stage profiles.
items.detail: EBRL’s scheduler overlaps rollout (simulation and action generation) with training, removing the previous GPU allocation barrier. The resource manager pools CPU cores and GPU streaming multiprocessors, using runtime feedback to adjust allocations per stage. This eliminates synchronization stalls and improves overall hardware utilization.

items.title: GLASS: Architecture-Tuned, Composable, Device-Side Linear Algebra for Edge Robotics and Beyond
items.summary: GLASS is a header‑only CUDA library offering multiple device‑side linear‑algebra kernels, with placement choices that can vary up to 81×; 145 of 396 kernels differ between Jetson AGX Orin and RTX 5090.
items.detail: GLASS selects the optimal implementation for each linear‑algebra primitive at compile time based on offline measurements. Placement decisions differ dramatically across hardware, with up to an 81× performance gap. The library’s header‑only design enables easy integration into edge‑robotics projects.

items.title: Distributed Stochastic Approximation Algorithms and Heavy-Tailed Age of Information
items.summary: The authors provide the first analysis of distributed stochastic approximation algorithms under heavy‑tailed Age‑of‑Information distributions that may have infinite mean.
items.detail: The analysis models Age‑of‑Information as a heavy‑tailed random variable, allowing infinite mean scenarios common in obstructed environments. It proves almost‑sure boundedness of the distributed iterates despite the lack of moment guarantees. This bridges the gap between theoretical assumptions and real‑world robotic swarm deployments.

items.title: From PyTorch to the NPU: LLM-Agent-Driven Model Conversion Across Heterogeneous Inference Runtimes
items.summary: The paper extends the LLM‑agent‑driven AIPC methodology to automate model conversion for heterogeneous edge inference runtimes, including Intel OpenVINO, Rockchip RKNN, NVIDIA TensorRT, and ONNX Runtime.
items.detail: The extended AIPC framework treats each target runtime as a separate deployment pipeline, automatically handling model conversion, operator mapping, and precision checks. An LLM agent orchestrates the process, reducing manual engineering effort across Intel OpenVINO, Rockchip RKNN, NVIDIA TensorRT, and ONNX Runtime.

items.title: DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp
items.summary: DeusData’s codebase‑memory‑mcp is a single‑binary code‑intelligence server that indexes repositories in milliseconds, supports 158 languages, and answers queries in sub‑millisecond latency with 99% fewer tokens.
items.detail: The server builds a persistent knowledge graph of code entities, enabling sub‑millisecond query responses. Indexing completes in a few milliseconds even for large repositories, and token usage drops by 99% compared to traditional approaches. It ships as a single static binary with no external dependencies.

items.title: XRPLF/rippled
items.summary: rippled is the C++ daemon that implements the XRP Ledger protocol for a decentralized cryptocurrency blockchain.
items.detail: rippled implements the full XRP Ledger consensus and transaction processing logic. It is used by validators and developers to run and test the decentralized ledger. The project is open source and written in modern C++.

items.title: acsandmann/rift
items.summary: rift is a tiling window manager for macOS.
items.detail: The project is hosted on GitHub and provides keyboard‑driven window arrangement on a platform that lacks native tiling. It is open‑source and targets users who prefer a more configurable desktop experience.

items.title: astral-sh/ruff
items.summary: ruff is an extremely fast Python linter and code formatter written in Rust.
items.detail: Ruff aims to replace tools like flake8 by running lint checks in parallel, offering significant speed gains. It is open‑source on GitHub and can be used as a drop‑in replacement in existing Python workflows.

items.title: bambulab/BambuStudio
items.summary: BambuStudio is PC software for controlling BambuLab and other 3D printers.
items.detail: The application, written in C++, provides slicing, printer management, and monitoring features across Windows, macOS, and Linux. It is open‑source and serves as the official desktop interface for BambuLab devices.

items.title: dail8859/NotepadNext
items.summary: NotepadNext is a cross‑platform reimplementation of Notepad++.
items.detail: Implemented in C++, NotepadNext brings the familiar Notepad++ editing experience to macOS and Linux, aiming for feature parity while using modern toolkits for native look and feel. The source is available on GitHub.
